items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: so I’ve toured a lot in Europe with him and he’s one of the best clarinetists I’ve worked with.

ctx.x: It’s interesting, we talked, well you were here a few weeks ago and you mentioned that you were coming back, and playing Klezmer music. I got the impression you weren’t really sure what you were going to be doing or who was playing, and is that a sort of a typical situation that you find yourself in?

Sometimes you get band leaders that will tell you every single detail, almost too much detail, and then you get the complete opposite where you’re not sure what time the gig is, where the gig is, if you’ll eat, where the hotel is. Sometimes you’re in the dark. But I’ve worked with David Krakauer, the artist tonight, on and off for the last ten years, mostly in Europe because he’s actually a big star in France. He had — a French record label put out a lot of records in France, so I’ve toured a lot in Europe with…
Is the music more popular over there? His kind of music?
